- Overestimate prices after recent spikes, especially when sentiment is high (≥0.75) — reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is low (≤0.33) — add 3–5% to forecast to account for potential rebound.
- If 3+ consecutive forecast days show upward trend with sentiment >0.6, apply mean reversion correction: subtract 1–2% from next 2–3 days.
- When sentiment drops sharply (e.g., from 0.8 to 0.2) and forecast is rising, reduce forecast by 5–8% to avoid overreaction.
- For 30-day forecasts, if last 5 days of forecast are >+3% above true, cap future forecast at 1–2% above recent 5-day average.
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., 0.8, 0.2, 0.8), adjust forecast to reflect sentiment volatility — avoid overfitting to recent trend.
